title: Portrait of an unknown Roman (sometimes identified as Crassus — unverified)
description: Several late Republican portrait busts have been tentatively identified as Crassus, but no verifiable contemporary portrait of Crassus survives. The so-called 'Crassus' in the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek (Copenhagen) is a late Republican veristic portrait, but the identification is speculative and lacks epigraphic confirmation. No securely identified portrait of Crassus exists.
location: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek, Copenhagen (tentative). Multiple museums have unverified identifications.
note: Unlike Caesar, Pompey, and Cicero, Crassus has no securely identified portrait. His coin imagery is minimal compared to contemporaries. This gap reflects his relatively brief military commands and his death before the triumviral coinage period.

title: Map of the Parthian campaign and Battle of Carrhae
description: Reconstructed route of Crassus's Parthian campaign from Syria across the Euphrates to Carrhae (modern Harran, Turkey). The route follows the Balikh River valley. Modern maps combine Plutarch's and Cassius Dio's narratives with archaeological topography.
note: Modern reconstruction, not a contemporary Roman military map. The Roman army's route and the battle site are identified through textual sources and archaeological survey.
